title: Existence of an integral basis for a finite extension of local coefficient fields
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime and let $E\subseteq F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], with the compatible absolute values extending the $\ell$-adic absolute value. Put $\mathcal O_E=\{x\in E:|x|\leq1\}$ and $\mathcal O_F=\{x\in F:|x|\leq1\}$, the rings of integers, with the inclusion induced by $E\subseteq F$. Let $d=[F:E]=\dim_E F$. There exist elements $b_1,\ldots,b_d\in\mathcal O_F$ such that every $x\in\mathcal O_F$ has a unique expression $x=\sum_{i=1}^d a_i b_i$ with $a_i\in\mathcal O_E$.

mathlib_candidate.how: Lines 175, 183, 192 give generic finite/free/rank results for integral closures. Applying them requires a theorem identifying the absolute-value ring of integers O_F with the integral closure of O_E in F, and the DVR/fraction-field/separability hypotheses. This bridge is not a one-line specialization, so this is not a Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$. The DVR theorem [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], applied to the spectral absolute value, gives that $E$ is its fraction field and that $A$ is a PID [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], $A$ is Noetherian and integrally closed. The field $E$ has characteristic zero since the map from $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] is injective, so its finite field extension $F$ is separable. All scalar maps used below are the composite $A\to E\to F$.

proof.text: Construct $C$ as the integral closure of $A$ in $F$. By [lem-sfb-padic-integers-integral-closure], applied to the canonical $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra map $E\to F$, membership in $C$ is equivalent to membership in $\mathcal O_F$. No witness of an arbitrary existence assertion is selected to define this algebra.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite], $C$ is finite over $A$. As a subalgebra of the field $F$ it is torsion-free over $A$, so the PID version of [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] makes it free. In Lean these conclusions are IsIntegralClosure.finite and IsIntegralClosure.module_free.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-integral-closure-rank] to obtain $\operatorname{finrank}_A C=\operatorname{finrank}_E F$. Choose the finite free basis with this index set, using Module.finBasisOfFinrankEq and [def-weil-vector-space-dimension].

source.place: Opening sentence, the clause of rank d; generic integral-closure rank calculation implemented by Mathlib/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/IntegralClosure.lean:192-200.

proof.text: For this basis $b$, take its images in $F$. They lie in $\mathcal O_F$ by step 2. For $x\in\mathcal O_F$, view it as $y\in C$ and set $a_i$ to the image in $E$ of $(b.\mathrm{repr}\,y)_i\in A$. Applying the inclusion $C\to F$ to the basis expansion gives $x=\sum_i\operatorname{algebraMap}_{E,F}(a_i)b_i$. Any other integral tuple defines $c_i\in A$ with $\sum_i c_i b_i=y$; apply b.repr and then evaluate at each index to recover $c_i=(b.\mathrm{repr}\,y)_i$. Taking the images in $E$ proves equality of tuples and hence uniqueness.
